title: Ordinary scalar realization of the specified older integral and raw rational stages
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $D=(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, an arbitrary scheme $Y$, finite extensions $E,F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a $\mathbf Q_\ell$-algebra map $i:E\to F$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On the small pro-etale site of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $R_H=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(\mathcal O_H/\varpi_H^n)_Y$ for $H=E,F$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $\widehat i:R_E\to R_F$ be the published completed coefficient map induced on finite quotient projections. Use sheaves of modules, their sheafified tensor product and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Let $\mathcal A_H^{\rm old}$ be exactly $\mathrm{boundedConstructibleDerivedCompleteIntegralCategory}(D,\ell,\ell\ne p,H,Y)$: the full category of derived-complete complexes whose specified $\mathrm{integralDerivedReduction}$ at every positive level is finite-torsion constructible, with a single finite cohomological support interval independent of the level [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Put $C_H^{\rm old}=\mathcal A_H^{\rm old}[1/\varpi_H]$, the raw Hom tensor localization with unchanged objects [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi]. Write $I_i$ for the published completed integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension] restricted to these older categories, and $T_i=\mathrm{rationalScalarExtension}(D,\ell,\ell\ne p,E,Y,F,i)$.

The ordinary module-sheaf functor $B_i=R_F\otimes_{R_E}-$ is additive and exact. Its termwise unbounded derived functor $D(B_i)=\mathrm{integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar}(\ell,E,F,i,Y)$ preserves these specified older full subcategories. Denote its restriction by $J_i=\mathrm{integralConstructibleScalarExtension}(D,\ell,\ell\ne p,E,F,i,Y)$. There is a unique natural isomorphism $\sigma_i:J_i\xrightarrow{\sim}I_i$ with the published quotient-completion normalization: on every flat-term K-flat complex [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] representing an object of $\mathcal A_E^{\rm old}$, after the completed representative comparison, its component is the ordinary derived factorization followed by the localization of the map to the strict product-cone scalar tower having all finite quotient tensor projections and zero shifted-product coordinate.

The raw scalar localization of $J_i$ is $S_i=\mathrm{rationalOrdinaryScalarExtension}(D,\ell,\ell\ne p,E,Y,F,i)$: on objects it is $J_i$ and on pure Hom tensors it sends $f\otimes e$ to $J_i(f)\otimes i(e)$. There is a unique natural isomorphism $c_i=\mathrm{rationalOrdinaryComparison}(D,\ell,\ell\ne p,E,Y,F,i):S_i\xrightarrow{\sim}T_i$ whose component at every integral object $K$ is the localized component $\sigma_{i,K}\otimes1$, with the specified endpoint equalities. These assertions include identity coefficient maps and do not identify the older integral predicate with any other integral presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-completed-integral-finite-free] to the published map $\widehat i$: its finite projection equations are precisely the hypothesis of that theorem. It gives an $R_E$-linear basis of $R_F$ of rank $[F:E]$. A field homomorphism $i$ is injective, so the finite-extension statements written for inclusions apply to its image, with the coefficient identifications induced by $i$. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-finite-free-scalar-coordinates] to this basis. Thus $B_i$ is exact and its termwise functor computes ordinary derived scalar extension on all unbounded complexes. Additivity follows directly from $1\otimes(f+g)(x)=1\otimes f(x)+1\otimes g(x)$ and the tensor relations [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The exact-functor factorization [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] identifies $D(B_i)(QP)$ with $Q(B_iP)$ by its specified factorization map, which is the published integralOrdinaryDerivedScalar construction.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1); ordinary tensor realization of blueprint scalar-extension proof (4); exact-functor factorization on cochain representatives.

proof.text: Take the ambient normalized transformation $\chi_i:D(B_i)\to\text{integralScalarExtension}_i$ of [lem-weil-normalized-scalar-completion]. For $K\in\mathcal A_E^{\rm old}$, derived completeness is its first defining condition [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], so $\chi_{i,K}$ is invertible. The completed image belongs to exactly the category defined by the same reductions and the uniform support interval, by [lem-weil-integral-scalar-extension-constructible]. Closure of this full subcategory under isomorphisms [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] therefore puts $D(B_i)K$ in $\mathcal A_F^{\rm old}$. Restrict the ordinary functor to obtain $J_i$. Fullness restricts $\chi_i$ and its inverse to a natural isomorphism $\sigma_i:J_i\cong I_i$. Its good-representative equation is the normalization of $\chi_i$, with precisely the ordinary factorization, finite quotient tensor projections and zero shifted-product coordinate. This uses the older predicate as stated; it does not pass through another integral constructibility predicate.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1 and Lemma 6.8.2(1); restrict the quotient-normalized comparison to the specified full subcategories.

proof.text: For uniqueness, let $\sigma'_i$ satisfy the same normalization. Given any $K\in\mathcal A_E^{\rm old}$, [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] supplies a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ and an isomorphism $e:QP\cong K$. Isomorphism closure [lem-weil-integral-constructible-triangulated] makes $QP$ an object of the older category. The two normalization equations at $P$ have the same right-hand side [lem-weil-normalized-scalar-completion]. Cancel the invertible completed representative comparison to get $\sigma'_{i,QP}=\sigma_{i,QP}$. Naturality with $e$ gives $\sigma'_{i,K}=I_i(e)\,\sigma_{i,QP}\,J_i(e)^{-1}=\sigma_{i,K}$. Equality of all components proves uniqueness of the natural isomorphism.

source.place: Proposition 3.5.1; good representative normalization and transport along a K-flat resolution.

proof.text: The ordinary tensor relations give $B_i(af)=i(a)B_i(f)$ for $a\in\mathcal O_E$: on a pure tensor both maps send $s\otimes x$ to $s\otimes af(x)=i(a)s\otimes f(x)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The same equality holds termwise and, since the localization functors are linear for the induced actions [lem-weil-linear-abelian-derived-category], after localization (also for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms); the $\mathcal O_E$- and $\mathcal O_F$-actions on the derived categories and on the older full subcategories are those through constant sections [lem-weil-integral-constructible-linear], and $\widehat i$ sends the constant section $a$ to the constant section $i(a)$ because it commutes with every finite quotient projection. Hence $J_i$ is $\mathcal O_E$-linear through $i$. In the raw Hom tensor localization [def-weil-linear-scalar-localization, def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], define $S_i(f\otimes e)=J_i(f)\otimes i(e)$. This respects the balancing relation because $J_i(af)\otimes i(e)=J_i(f)\otimes i(ae)$, and it is additive in both variables. Tensor bilinearity makes it a unique additive map on each Hom group. It preserves identities since $J_i(1)\otimes i(1)=1\otimes1$; on two pure tensors preservation of composition is $J_i(gf)\otimes i(de)=(J_i(g)\otimes i(d))(J_i(f)\otimes i(e))$, and distributivity proves it for sums. This is exactly the published rationalOrdinaryScalarExtension, with unchanged raw-localization objects.

source.place: Step (4), ordinary scalar tensor realization; retained raw rational Hom construction, RationalizationKaroubi.lean:210-264.

proof.text: Set $c_{i,K}=\sigma_{i,K}\otimes1$ in the raw target Hom group [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi, def-weil-linear-scalar-localization]. The published $T_i$ uses $I_i$ on integral objects and $I_i(f)\otimes i(e)$ on pure Hom tensors. For such a tensor, the naturality square is the integral equation $I_i(f)\sigma_{i,K}=\sigma_{i,M}J_i(f)$ multiplied by $i(e)$; every Hom tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, so additivity gives naturality everywhere. The components $\sigma_{i,K}^{-1}\otimes1$ give the inverse, as both composites are $1\otimes1$. Every raw object is an integral object, so the required component formula fixes the entire natural isomorphism and proves uniqueness, with precisely the specified endpoints. For $i=1_E$ these arguments still use the normalized completeness comparison, not an asserted literal identity for $I_i$; all formulas remain valid. Zero objects and the empty scheme require no separate choices.
